content: The most common types of bariatric surgery include Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) and sleeve gastrectomy. These procedures involve the creation of smaller stomach pouches, which limit the amount of food a patient can consume and induce changes in the digestive process. Clinical evidence indicates that both RYGB and sleeve gastrectomy are effective in promoting diabetes remission in 30% to 63% of patients within one to five years following surgery. For sustained long-term outcomes, many patients experience continued improvements in blood glucose regulation. Research has shown that after five years, 29% of patients maintain hemoglobin A1C levels below 6%, reflecting excellent glycemic control.
